subject: Multi-year commit: proposed invoice split and revenue recognition notes
participants_external: emma.li@horizonai.com (Emma Li, Head of Finance, HorizonAI)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@horizonai.com>, purchasing@horizonai.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial proposal: multi-year commit + invoicing approach

Emma / Horizon team —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Per our conversation, attached is a draft SOW that reflects the 3-year committed capacity (1.2M tokens/month baseline, burst pool) and the term pricing we discussed (12% discount year 1, 7% year 2, 5% year 3).

Two operational asks from your side that I want to confirm up front:
- You asked about splitting the prepay invoice across fiscal years so your finance team can match spend to budget. We can do a per-year invoice (Year 1 invoice at signing, Year 2 and Year 3 invoiced annually in advance on the contract anniversary), or we can issue the full prepay up front and provide credit memos.
- You also asked about any documentation Redwood can provide for revenue recognition purposes — short note on deliverables and the billing schedule.

Attached: SOW + a proposed invoice split spreadsheet (tab: option A = annual prepay; option B = front-loaded with credit schedule).

Next steps: if annual prepay invoices work, I can confirm the exact dates and will loop in Marissa from Finance to finalize wording for the order form. If your procurement prefers a single up-front payment with credits, we should get legal eyes on how the credits are documented so it doesn't create recognition ambiguity on your side.

Would love to lock this by the end of next week if possible.

Best,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: HorizonAI_MultiYear_SOW_2026.pdf, commit-invoice-schedule-v2.xlsx

From: Emma Li <emma.li@horizonai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: purchasing@horizonai.com, Devin Ross <devin.ross@horizonai.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: multi-year commit + invoicing approach

Sean —

Thanks for the SOW and the two invoicing options. Quick answers from our side:
- Preferred: split invoices by fiscal year (we close books on 12/31). So Year 1: invoice on signing (we will pay within our standard 30 days). Year 2 and Year 3: invoice on each anniversary and we will set the payments against those fiscal years.
- For rev-rec: we need a short vendor statement that lists the services being provided (inference capacity, support hours, dedicated SLA) and confirms that the annual invoices correspond to a year of service. That helps our accounting classify as prepaid service and amortize over the year.

Also looping Devin for legal — we may require a 30-day payment term in the order form and a clause stating that unused prepaid capacity does not carry beyond the term unless explicitly rolled forward.

Can you circulate a version of the invoice schedule that shows invoice dates and a one-paragraph rev-rec statement for our records?

Thanks,
Emma
Head of Finance, HorizonAI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: HorizonAI — invoice split + rev-rec ask (need guidance)

Team — forwarding Horizon's note. Key asks: annual invoices aligned to their fiscal year, 30-day payment terms acceptable, and they want a one-paragraph rev-rec vendor statement confirming the invoice maps to a year of service.

Questions for Finance/Legal:
- Marissa: can Redwood issue three separate annual prepay invoices (each invoiced in advance on the anniversary) while still classifying revenue under ASC 606 correctly? What memo do we need to provide Horizon to satisfy their auditors?
- Karthik: anything we should add to the order form about unused capacity / rollover limitations to avoid surprises later?

I included Laura as well to ensure CS/Delivery are comfortable with the stated deliverables in the SOW.

Thanks,
Sean

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HorizonAI — invoice split + rev-rec ask (need guidance)

Sean / team —

We can accommodate the annual-in-advance invoices per Horizon's request. Internal notes and recommended approach:

1) Invoicing mechanics (preferred):
- Issue Year 1 invoice at signing (covers service period: signing date -> signing date + 12 months).
- Issue Year 2 invoice on the contract anniversary for service period year 2, and Year 3 similarly.
- Payment terms: Net 30 per Horizon request (documented on order form).

2) Revenue recognition (high level):
- Redwood should recognize revenue ratably over each 12-month service period covered by an invoice (i.e., amortize the prepaid invoice as deferred revenue and release monthly). This aligns to ASC 606 guidance for subscription-like service.
- Provide a one-page vendor attestation stating: (a) the invoice is for prepaid access to inference capacity and support for the stated 12-month period, (b) Redwood delivers continuous access and support per SOW, and (c) Redwood will recognize revenue ratably across the service period. We can include a single-paragraph statement in a PDF (revrec-clearance-note-Redwood.pdf).

3) Accounting impact considerations:
- If Horizon prefers a single up-front payment for all three years, we would record the full amount as deferred revenue and recognize it over 36 months. This is fine, but some customers prefer per-year invoices to match budgeting cycles — which Horizon indicated.
- Unused capacity language: recommend restricting rollover to explicit written agreement. Put a one-sentence cap in the order form: "Unused prepaid capacity expires at the end of each 12-month period unless otherwise agreed in writing." That keeps revenue recognition and deliverables clean.

I'll draft the vendor attestation and a small paragraph to drop into the order form. Sean — once you have Horizon's preferred invoice dates, I'll generate the PDFs and invoice schedule.

-Marissa
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: revrec-clearance-note-Redwood.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Final: confirmed invoice schedule + vendor rev-rec attestation

Emma / Horizon team —

Thanks for the clarity. Per your preference, attached is the invoice schedule showing three separate annual prepay invoices, with the first invoice issued on signing (we used 2026-06-01 as the target signing date for illustration) and subsequent invoices on each anniversary. Payment terms: Net 30.

Also attached is a one-paragraph vendor attestation that your accounting team can retain with the invoice to support revenue recognition. It states that each invoice corresponds to a 12-month prepaid service period and that Redwood will recognize revenue ratably over that period.

Key points we captured:
- Unused prepaid capacity does not auto-rollover and expires at the end of each 12-month term unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- If Horizon requests an alternative billing (single up-front payment), Redwood will provide a revised rev-rec note indicating amortization over the full prepaid period.

Attachments: HorizonAI_MultiYear_SOW_2026.pdf, commit-invoice-schedule-v2.xlsx, revrec-clearance-note-Redwood.pdf

If this aligns with your requirements, can you confirm and we will prepare the final order form and intake for signature?

Best,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
